chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from al-Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'Does that matter have a specific time?' He said: 'The dividers of time are liars, the dividers of time are liars. Indeed, when Moses went as an envoy to his Lord and promised his people thirty days, and when Allah added ten days to the thirty, his people said: "Moses has broken his promise to us." So they did what they did. When we narrate a narration to you and it comes to pass as we narrated to you, say: "Allah has spoken the truth." And when we narrate a narration to you and it comes to pass contrary to what we narrated to you, say: "Allah has spoken the truth." You will be rewarded twice.'.

key_terms.أَخْلَفَنَا: He broke his promise to us
key_terms.الْوَقَاتُونَ: Those who fix specific times (for the appearance of the Imam)
key_terms.لِلْأَمْرِ وَقْتٌ: A specific time for the matter (the reappearance)

ai.seo_question: Why did the people of Moses accuse him of breaking his promise when Allah extended the time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the 'Waqatun' (those who fix times) by citing the incident of the Golden Calf, where the Israelites accused Moses of breaking his promise after Allah extended the thirty-day period by ten days. This hadith establishes the principle of 'delayed fulfillment' (Taqdim wa Ta'khir) in Shia eschatology, teaching that believers earn double reward for maintaining faith whether the event occurs precisely as predicted or with a divine delay.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from al-Husayn bin Muhammad from Mu’alla bin Muhammad from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Khazzaz from Abdul Kareem bin Amr al-Khath’ami that al-Fudhayl bin Yasar had said: “I asked Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) if that matter (the appearance of al-Qa’im) had a certain appointment

and he said: “The diviners tell lies! The diviners tell lies! When Prophet Moses (as) devoted himself to his Lord, he promised his people that after thirty days Allah would do away with their enemy. When Allah added ten days to the thirty, the people said that Moses had broken his promise and then they disbelieved and made a metallic calf as their god. When we tell you of something and Allah does as we have told you, you are to say that Allah has fulfilled His promise and when we tell you of something but a different thing occurs, also you are to say that Allah has fulfilled his promise. Then you will be rewarded twice.”
